---
title: "Pareto-smoothed importance sampling leave-one-out cross-validation"
---

The [exact LOO page](leave-one-out-cross-validation.qmd) computed every omitted-position posterior directly under a conjugate Provo model. [**Pareto-smoothed importance sampling leave-one-out cross-validation (PSIS-LOO)**](https://mc-stan.org/loo/articles/online-only/faq.html) approximates those omitted-data posteriors using draws from the posterior fit to all observations. It applies the reweighting operation introduced on the [importance-sampling page](../statistical-inference/importance-sampling.qmd#reweighting-a-proposal). Because exact values are available here, approximation error becomes observable. We proceed in three steps: first, we derive the inverse-likelihood ratio; second, we show how Pareto smoothing modifies its tail; finally, we compare the approximation with exact LOO on the same Provo positions.

The [posterior distribution page](../statistical-inference/posterior-distributions.qmd) defines the conditional target represented by the full data draws, and the [likelihood page](../statistical-inference/maximum-likelihood.qmd#probability-and-likelihood) defines the pointwise contribution removed by LOO. The [Provo data discussion](likelihood-ratio-tests.qmd#provo-data) fixes that contribution as one aggregated content word position, so PSIS does not silently change the prediction target to a reader or passage.

## Exact Bayesian leave-one-out prediction

Let $y_{-i}$ contain all responses except $y_i$. Given a factorized likelihood and prior density $f(\theta)$,

$$
f(\theta\mid y_{-i})
\propto
f(\theta)\prod_{j\neq i}f(y_j\mid\theta).
$$

The exact predictive density is

$$
f(y_i\mid y_{-i})
=
\int f(y_i\mid\theta)f(\theta\mid y_{-i})\,\mathrm d\theta.
$$

Summing its logarithm gives expected log pointwise predictive density:

$$
\operatorname{elpd}_{\mathrm{loo}}
=
\sum_{i=1}^N\log f(y_i\mid y_{-i}).
$$

Larger values indicate greater predictive density for the omitted positions.

## Relating the omitted posterior to the full posterior

Given draws $\theta^{(1)},\ldots,\theta^{(S)}$ from

$$
f(\theta\mid y)
\propto
f(\theta)\prod_{j=1}^Nf(y_j\mid\theta),
$$

removing the $i$th contribution gives

$$
f(\theta\mid y_{-i})
\propto
\frac{f(\theta\mid y)}{f(y_i\mid\theta)}.
$$

The raw importance ratio is consequently

$$
r_i^{(s)}\propto\frac{1}{f(y_i\mid\theta^{(s)})}.
$$

This inverse weighting is both the shortcut and its weakness. A few enormous ratios can make full-posterior draws a poor representation of the omitted posterior.

Normalize the ratios within position $i$:

$$
w_i^{(s)}
=
\frac{r_i^{(s)}}{\sum_{t=1}^S r_i^{(t)}}.
$$

The importance-sampling estimate of the omitted predictive density is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat f(y_i\mid y_{-i})
&=
\sum_{s=1}^S w_i^{(s)}f(y_i\mid\theta^{(s)})\\
&=
\frac{\sum_s f(y_i\mid\theta^{(s)})/f(y_i\mid\theta^{(s)})}
{\sum_s 1/f(y_i\mid\theta^{(s)})}\\
&=
\left[
\frac1S\sum_{s=1}^S\frac{1}{f(y_i\mid\theta^{(s)})}
\right]^{-1}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus raw importance sampling produces a harmonic-mean form. The same cancellation
that makes the expression simple makes it sensitive to a draw assigning tiny
likelihood to $y_i$.

## Pareto-smoothing the importance ratios {#pareto-smoothing-the-importance-ratios}

PSIS orders the raw ratios for position $i$ and treats the largest ratios as a tail
sample. It fits a generalized Pareto distribution to that tail, replaces the ordered
extremes with fitted Pareto quantiles, and applies a finite-sample truncation rule so
one smoothed ratio cannot dominate without bound. The smaller ratios remain
unchanged. The resulting ratios are normalized and used in the same weighted
predictive-density calculation.

The fitted tail shape $k$ summarizes how heavy the ratio tail is. In the idealized
Pareto model, a moment of order $m$ exists only when $k<1/m$: [variance](../random-variables-and-distributions/variance-and-covariance.qmd) requires
$k<1/2$, while the mean requires $k<1$. The plotted 0.7 line is a practical
finite-sample warning threshold used by the implementation, not a new moment
boundary or a data-exclusion rule. A position above it calls for checking exact
refitting, moment matching, or another validation design.

The [**Pareto $k$ diagnostic**](https://mc-stan.org/loo/reference/pareto-k-diagnostic.html) reports that fitted tail shape for each position. Large $k$ warns about the approximation; it does not establish that an observation is erroneous or should be removed.

## PSIS and exact LOO on the same Provo positions

The code reloads the [Provo position table](likelihood-ratio-tests.qmd#provo-data), reconstructs the fixed study-calibrated priors, draws independently from both conjugate posteriors, and preserves one log likelihood column per position. It also recomputes exact LOO so the PSIS totals can be checked directly. The [normal inverse gamma update](leave-one-out-cross-validation.qmd#normal-inverse-gamma-posterior-and-predictive-update) supplies `Vn`, `bn`, `an`, and `dn`; this page reuses those quantities rather than defining a second posterior.

```{r}
#| label: provo-psis-loo
#| message: false
#| warning: false

provo <- utils::read.csv(
  "data/provo/content-word-positions.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
provo$cloze_surprisal_bits <- -log2(provo$OrthoMatchModel)
y <- provo$mean_log_ffd

linear_fit <- lm(
  mean_log_ffd ~ cloze_surprisal_bits,
  data = provo
)
quadratic_fit <- lm(
  mean_log_ffd ~ cloze_surprisal_bits + I(cloze_surprisal_bits^2),
  data = provo
)
X_linear <- model.matrix(linear_fit)
X_quadratic <- model.matrix(quadratic_fit)

make_prior <- function(X) {
  log_bounds <- log(c(80, 800))
  log_span <- diff(log_bounds)
  expected_sigma2 <- (log_span / 4)^2
  list(
    b0 = c(mean(log_bounds), rep(0, ncol(X) - 1L)),
    V0 = diag(rep(log_span^2 / expected_sigma2, ncol(X))),
    a0 = 3,
    d0 = 2 * expected_sigma2
  )
}

nig_posterior <- function(X, y, prior) {
  V0_inverse <- solve(prior$V0)
  Vn <- solve(V0_inverse + crossprod(X))
  bn <- drop(Vn %*% (
    V0_inverse %*% prior$b0 + crossprod(X, y)
  ))
  an <- prior$a0 + length(y) / 2
  dn <- as.numeric(
    prior$d0 + 0.5 * (
      crossprod(y) +
        t(prior$b0) %*% V0_inverse %*% prior$b0 -
        t(bn) %*% solve(Vn) %*% bn
    )
  )
  list(Vn = Vn, bn = bn, an = an, dn = dn)
}

draw_nig <- function(posterior, draws, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  sigma2 <- 1 / rgamma(
    draws, shape = posterior$an, rate = posterior$dn
  )
  standard_normal <- matrix(
    rnorm(draws * length(posterior$bn)), nrow = draws
  )
  beta <- matrix(
    posterior$bn,
    nrow = draws,
    ncol = length(posterior$bn),
    byrow = TRUE
  ) + sweep(
    standard_normal %*% chol(posterior$Vn),
    1,
    sqrt(sigma2),
    "*"
  )
  list(beta = beta, sigma2 = sigma2)
}

log_likelihood_matrix <- function(X, y, draws) {
  mu <- draws$beta %*% t(X)
  standardized <- sweep(mu, 2, y, "-")
  standardized <- sweep(
    standardized, 1, sqrt(draws$sigma2), "/"
  )
  -0.5 * log(2 * pi) - 0.5 * log(draws$sigma2) -
    0.5 * standardized^2
}

exact_nig_loo <- function(X, y, prior) {
  n <- nrow(X)
  V0_inverse <- solve(prior$V0)
  full_xtx <- crossprod(X)
  full_xty <- crossprod(X, y)
  full_yty <- sum(y^2)
  log_density <- numeric(n)

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    xi <- matrix(X[i, ], nrow = 1L)
    yi <- y[i]
    Vn <- solve(V0_inverse + full_xtx - crossprod(xi))
    bn <- drop(Vn %*% (
      V0_inverse %*% prior$b0 + full_xty - drop(xi) * yi
    ))
    an <- prior$a0 + (n - 1L) / 2
    dn <- as.numeric(
      prior$d0 + 0.5 * (
        full_yty - yi^2 +
          t(prior$b0) %*% V0_inverse %*% prior$b0 -
          t(bn) %*% solve(Vn) %*% bn
      )
    )
    location <- drop(xi %*% bn)
    scale <- sqrt(
      (dn / an) * (1 + drop(xi %*% Vn %*% t(xi)))
    )
    degrees <- 2 * an
    log_density[i] <-
      dt((yi - location) / scale, df = degrees, log = TRUE) -
      log(scale)
  }
  log_density
}

linear_prior <- make_prior(X_linear)
quadratic_prior <- make_prior(X_quadratic)
linear_posterior <- nig_posterior(X_linear, y, linear_prior)
quadratic_posterior <- nig_posterior(
  X_quadratic, y, quadratic_prior
)

posterior_draws <- 4000L
linear_draws <- draw_nig(
  linear_posterior, posterior_draws, seed = 20261104
)
quadratic_draws <- draw_nig(
  quadratic_posterior, posterior_draws, seed = 20261105
)
linear_log_lik <- log_likelihood_matrix(
  X_linear, y, linear_draws
)
quadratic_log_lik <- log_likelihood_matrix(
  X_quadratic, y, quadratic_draws
)

linear_psis <- loo::loo(
  linear_log_lik, r_eff = rep(1, ncol(linear_log_lik))
)
quadratic_psis <- loo::loo(
  quadratic_log_lik,
  r_eff = rep(1, ncol(quadratic_log_lik))
)
linear_k <- loo::pareto_k_values(linear_psis)
quadratic_k <- loo::pareto_k_values(quadratic_psis)

linear_exact <- sum(exact_nig_loo(X_linear, y, linear_prior))
quadratic_exact <- sum(exact_nig_loo(
  X_quadratic, y, quadratic_prior
))

psis_summary <- data.frame(
  model = c("Linear", "Quadratic"),
  psis_elpd_loo = c(
    linear_psis$estimates["elpd_loo", "Estimate"],
    quadratic_psis$estimates["elpd_loo", "Estimate"]
  ),
  exact_elpd_loo = c(linear_exact, quadratic_exact),
  max_pareto_k = c(max(linear_k), max(quadratic_k)),
  positions_k_over_threshold = c(
    sum(linear_k > 0.7), sum(quadratic_k > 0.7)
  )
)
psis_summary$psis_minus_exact <- with(
  psis_summary, psis_elpd_loo - exact_elpd_loo
)
psis_summary

pareto_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    surprisal = provo$cloze_surprisal_bits,
    model = "Linear",
    pareto_k = linear_k
  ),
  data.frame(
    surprisal = provo$cloze_surprisal_bits,
    model = "Quadratic",
    pareto_k = quadratic_k
  )
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  pareto_data,
  ggplot2::aes(surprisal, pareto_k)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0.7,
    color = "grey55",
    linewidth = 0.45,
    linetype = 2
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 0.7, alpha = 0.35, color = "grey25") + # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ model) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Modeled cloze surprisal (bits)",
    y = "Pareto k"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11)
```

The posterior draws are generated independently, so the relative effective sample size is one for every position. An [effective sample size](../statistical-inference/effective-sample-size.qmd#from-autocorrelation-to-ess) translates dependence among simulation draws into the independent-draw count with comparable Monte Carlo variance. Because these draws do not form an autocorrelated [Markov chain](../statistical-inference/markov-chains.qmd#the-markov-property), `r_eff = 1`; that value says nothing about the number of independent Provo passages or readers. PSIS-LOO gives ELPD `r sprintf("%.3f", psis_summary$psis_elpd_loo[psis_summary$model == "Linear"])` for the linear model and `r sprintf("%.3f", psis_summary$psis_elpd_loo[psis_summary$model == "Quadratic"])` for the quadratic model. The differences from exact conjugate LOO are `r sprintf("%.3f", psis_summary$psis_minus_exact[psis_summary$model == "Linear"])` and `r sprintf("%.3f", psis_summary$psis_minus_exact[psis_summary$model == "Quadratic"])`.

The 4,000 draws are a computational accuracy choice: more independent draws reduce
[Monte Carlo variation](../statistical-inference/monte-carlo-integration.qmd#two-uncertainties) in the log-mean calculations, while costing memory and time.
They are not 4,000 new Provo observations. Because `draw_nig()` samples directly and
independently from the conjugate posterior rather than producing an autocorrelated
Markov chain, the relative effective sample-size input is `r_eff = 1` for each
position.

Maximum Pareto $k$ is `r sprintf("%.3f", psis_summary$max_pareto_k[psis_summary$model == "Linear"])` for the linear model and `r sprintf("%.3f", psis_summary$max_pareto_k[psis_summary$model == "Quadratic"])` for the quadratic model. `r sum(psis_summary$positions_k_over_threshold)` positions exceed the plotted reference value. Thus the approximation is accurate for this fitted pair, and the exact calculation provides the evidence for saying so.

The formula-to-code map is: each column of `linear_log_lik` or
`quadratic_log_lik` contains $\log f(y_i\mid\theta^{(s)})$ across draws; `loo::loo()`
constructs and smooths the inverse-likelihood ratios; `pareto_k_values()` returns one
tail diagnostic per column; and `exact_nig_loo()` provides the target against which
the approximation is checked.

## The pointwise likelihood fixes the target

The log-likelihood matrices have `r ncol(linear_log_lik)` position columns and `r nrow(linear_log_lik)` posterior-draw rows. A vector of total log likelihoods cannot support omission because it discards the pointwise contributions.

Default PSIS-LOO omits one such contribution. Here that contribution is one aggregated content-word position. Other positions from the same passage remain in the full posterior, so summing position scores by passage cannot create leave-one-passage-out validation. A new-passage target would require a grouped likelihood and validation design from the start.

When $k$ is large, responses include exact refitting, moment matching, or a different validation design. Removing the position solely because it is difficult would confuse a computational warning with a data-quality judgment.

## Checking the approximation

1. Why are raw importance ratios inversely related to the held-out likelihood contribution?
2. What does Pareto $k$ diagnose?
3. Why is exact LOO available as a decisive check in this example?
4. Which prediction target is fixed by one column of the log-likelihood matrix?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Removing $y_i$ divides the full posterior kernel by its likelihood contribution.
2. It diagnoses whether the importance-ratio tail is too heavy for stable
   full-posterior reweighting.
3. Conjugacy supplies the omitted-position Student-$t$ density without numerical
   refitting.
4. One aggregated content-word position, conditional on all remaining positions.

</details>

## Recap and forward link

1. Raw LOO importance sampling has a harmonic-mean form.
2. Pareto smoothing stabilizes the largest ratios and $k$ diagnoses their tail.
3. A likelihood column fixes the omitted unit.

The [previous page](leave-one-out-cross-validation.qmd#normal-inverse-gamma-posterior-and-predictive-update)
computed the exact target; the [next page](waic.qmd#fitted-posterior-predictive-density)
applies a posterior-variance correction to the same pointwise likelihood matrices.
